SEC’S RESPONSE TO GROUP 7 POSITION STATEMENTS
OF BMO, CITIBANK, AND SABAL CAPITAL OPERATIONS, LLC
The SEC hereby responds to the Group 7 Position Statements of BMO Bank N.A. (ECF
1794), Citibank N.A. (ECF 1797), and Sabal Capital Operations, LLC (ECF 1798). As discussed
below, because this Court and the Seventh Circuit have already addressed factually similar
priority disputes in favor of investors who had recorded mortgages that were never validly
released, the Court should find that such Group 7 investors likewise have priority.
A.  Citibank (Properties 69 and 73) and Sabal (Property 70) 1
In their Position Statements, Institutional Lenders Citibank and Sabal concede that for
Properties 69, 70, and 73: (a) investors obtained and recorded valid first-in-time mortgages, and
(b) no releases exist. (ECF 1797 at 2-4; ECF 1798 at 1-2). As the SEC’s Position Statement
(ECF 1795) notes, the Seventh Circuit has already determined that such facts readily answer the
1  Citibank and Sabal’s Position Statements are functionally identical, and themselves repeat the
same arguments of the Group 6 Position Statements of Midland (ECF 1757) and UBS (1756), all
of which were prepared by the same attorneys. Accordingly, the SEC’s response to Citibank and
Sabal advances the same arguments as its Group 6 Position Statement Response (ECF 1765).
